source.title: Tractatus de avertenda et profliganda peste politico-legalis
source.author: Girolamo Gastaldi
source.rightsNote: Original text and engravings published in 1684. Facsimiles are reproduced from the Google-digitized copy hosted by the Internet Archive; original scan marks and page content are retained. Cite the original edition and this digitized copy when reusing excerpts.
source.pageNumberingNote: Printed page numbers differ from PDF scan positions. Scan pages here are 1-based; Internet Archive n-page links use 0-based positions. Selected PDF pages are complete and uncropped.

excerpts.title: When one co-resident's illness report suffices
excerpts.description: The 24 August 1656 edict reaffirms illness reporting to district notaries and clarifies the exemption from duplicate reporting by co-residents about the same sick person.
excerpts.readingGuide: English paraphrase: report sick people even without signs or suspicion of contagion. Once one co-resident has reported the sick person, the others need not report that same person again. The edict recalls the 20 June proclamation reproduced in chapter 55.
excerpts.notes: Chapter XCIX begins below the ornament halfway down p. 370 and ends with the signatures Il Card. Sforza and Cesare Rasponi Secr. The text above the ornament belongs to chapter XCVIII. A complete transcription and English working translation are available on the chapter 99 page.
excerpts.explanationType: Analytical English paraphrase; original Italian/Latin remains visible in the facsimile

excerpts.title: Health passes, routes and discriminatory exclusions
excerpts.description: Rules for named health certificates, route endorsements, free issuance and forged or transferred documents, followed by explicit exclusions based on social and religious status.
excerpts.notes: Selected pages from chapter XLIII, not the entire chapter. These status exclusions are historical discriminatory rules, not evidence that the named groups carried infection.
excerpts.explanationType: Analytical English paraphrase; original Italian/Latin remains visible in the facsimile
excerpts.readingGuide: English paraphrase: certificates must identify each traveller and be endorsed along the journey; they must be issued free. Page 281 excludes vagabonds, able-bodied beggars, Roma and Jews even if they hold health papers.

excerpts.title: Reporting illness and deaths
excerpts.description: An extensive order makes households, clergy and medical practitioners part of the reporting network, appoints district notaries, controls burials and possessions, and offers compensation for disclosed property.
excerpts.notes: The complete pages include the start of the following chapter on p. 301. This scan contains an earlier duplicate of pp. 297-298; this excerpt uses the continuous sequence at scan pages 381-385.
excerpts.explanationType: Analytical English paraphrase; original Italian/Latin remains visible in the facsimile
excerpts.readingGuide: English paraphrase: report household illness promptly, including illness that shows no sign of plague; physicians must provide signed daily returns, and suspected contagion must be reported without waiting until evening.

excerpts.title: Four people per tavern table
excerpts.description: A compact four-part decree restricts courtesan-house visits, roaming cats and dogs, tavern groups and nonessential visits to sick people.
excerpts.notes: The four-person cap applies to tavern tables, not to every gathering in Rome. Chapter CXXVI ends near the top of p. 418, which also begins the next tribunal-suspension order.
excerpts.explanationType: Analytical English paraphrase; original Italian/Latin remains visible in the facsimile
excerpts.readingGuide: English paraphrase: innkeepers may not seat more than four people at a table. Sick visits are limited to household members and specified necessary religious, clinical, legal and care roles unless permission is obtained.

excerpts.title: Disinfection without a charge
excerpts.description: An order denies rumours of expensive cleansing fees and requires treated belongings to be returned to owners who establish their title, without an expurgation payment.
excerpts.notes: Chapter CXLII ends on p. 447, where the next order begins. The text combines free service with coercion; it does not establish that every worker complied.
excerpts.explanationType: Analytical English paraphrase; original Italian/Latin remains visible in the facsimile
excerpts.readingGuide: English paraphrase: owners owe no cleansing fee, and disinfectors may not demand one. The same order retains severe penalties for hiding suspect property and rewards disclosure.

excerpts.title: Compensation and an amnesty for the ghetto
excerpts.description: A fifteen-day amnesty addresses concealed or untreated property. The order records the Jewish community leaders' offer to pay for deterioration caused by cleansing.
excerpts.notes: Chapter CCIX begins partway down p. 532. Compensation follows an offer by the community's leaders; it should not be described as an unconditional treasury payment to all Romans.
excerpts.explanationType: Analytical English paraphrase; original Italian/Latin remains visible in the facsimile
excerpts.readingGuide: English paraphrase: value belongings before treatment and compensate their owners from community funds for damage, or allow a voluntary sale to the community at the assessed value. Gastaldi supervises cleansing and purchase.

excerpts.title: Separate cohorts and contact-free meals
excerpts.description: Instructions for the internal superintendent of San Pancrazio address accommodation, support for poor residents, separation by time in quarantine, food deliveries, cleaning and records.
excerpts.notes: The cohort and meal procedure appears on p. 582. The same instructions distinguish accommodation by social rank and provide food tickets for those unable to pay.
excerpts.explanationType: Analytical English paraphrase; original Italian/Latin remains visible in the facsimile
excerpts.readingGuide: English paraphrase: people who have already spent longer in quarantine should not mix with more recent arrivals. Residents put vessels outside their rooms, withdraw while food is served, and collect it after a signal.

excerpts.title: Two teams for cleansing infected houses
excerpts.description: A detailed protocol separates exposed and clean workers, specifies protective clothing, sequences washing and fumigation, includes places used before illness, and delays reoccupation.
excerpts.notes: Chapter CCXLII ends near the top of p. 619, followed by another cleansing protocol. This is historical prescription, not current medical or chemical-safety guidance.
excerpts.explanationType: Analytical English paraphrase; original Italian/Latin remains visible in the facsimile
excerpts.readingGuide: English paraphrase: 'dirty' workers perform the initial treatment; 'clean' workers finish the process without mixing with them. The protocol calls for at least fifteen days from the first operation to reoccupation, with specified ventilation and fumigation intervals.

excerpts.title: Reopening after sustained health assurance
excerpts.description: The final collected edict restores commerce to named towns after elapsed disease-free periods while continuing to control household textiles, furniture and other merchandise.
excerpts.notes: Chapter CCXXVII begins partway down p. 555. The date on p. 556 shows that the documentary sequence extends beyond calendar 1657.
excerpts.explanationType: Analytical English paraphrase; original Italian/Latin remains visible in the facsimile
excerpts.readingGuide: English paraphrase: reopen movement of people and specified necessities after the recorded last cases and periods of health assurance; require local permission for other household goods. The order is dated 1 March 1658.

excerpts.title: Trastevere and Tiber Island: the containment landscape
excerpts.description: The original engraved plan depicts the enclosed Trastevere district and Tiber Island, used as an infected-person lazaretto, with lettered features explained in chapter XXVII.
excerpts.notes: The PDF preserves the sideways source page in full. Browser images are rotated for reading, with no content removed. The surrounding explanation is on printed pp. 177-178.
excerpts.explanationType: Analytical English paraphrase; original Italian/Latin remains visible in the facsimile
excerpts.readingGuide: English paraphrase of the plate heading: topography of the enclosed Trastevere district and Tiber Island.

hero.alt: Engraved 1684 plan of the enclosed Trastevere district and Tiber Island in Rome, with streets, walls, river and lettered health-control features.
hero.caption: Trastevere and Tiber Island. Gastaldi, 1684, chapter XXVII, printed p. 179; scan page 259. Rendered upright from the original engraving.
